public_rationale: OpenAI’s February 15, 2024 disclosure describes training Sora on videos paired with generated text captions [e3]. On March 6, 2024, The Times of India quoted Rahul Agarwalla describing a Sora monkey-chess video with a 7×7 board and three kings [e4]. This supports the limited claim that this Sora system’s video-text training did not prevent the reported malformed chess scene [e3, e4].
limitations: The original video frames were not independently inspected; the dimensions and piece counts rely on the news report.
The report does not explain the counting procedure, establish independent inspection by the quoted expert, or distinguish kings on and off the board.
The evidence does not establish physical impossibility, the cause of the error, or a limitation applying to every system trained on paired videos and text.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Grounding in video-text relationships is not enough to prevent Sora from producing impossible outputs like 7x7 chessboards with 3 kings.

statement.excerpt: Sora is obviously grounded in relationships between videos and associated texts; yet that grounding is not enough to preclude 7x7 chessboards with 3 kings.

from_speaker: grounded in relationships between videos and associated texts
that grounding is not enough to preclude
our_interpretation: Grounding means training on videos associated with text descriptions.
This is a limited sufficiency claim: the actual trained Sora system can still produce the specified malformed chess scene.
It does not claim that video-text training causes the error or that every possible system using such training must fail.
The reference is the monkey-chess demonstration discussed in the post, not subsequent Sora versions.
criteria.support_condition: Training documentation establishes video-text association, and an authenticated output or reliable report identifies the specified seven-by-seven board and three kings in the referenced demonstration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable examination establishes that the referenced output was not generated by Sora or that the specified board and piece counts are mistaken.
